headline: High: OpenHands can write/egress by default while the paired awesome-list has no runtime surface, creating asymmetric leakage and conflict risks if any shared workspace or MCP bridge is introduced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A has no I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot ingest B's outputs directly. Profile B can use MCP, files, browser, and shell, so if an operator bridges A's content into B via copy/paste or a shared file, prompt injection becomes possible. The pathway is not default, so low fits.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B's prompt or files
IF B is connected to an MCP server that exposes A-controlled content
mitigations: Avoid copying untrusted text from A into B
Disable MCP servers unless needed
Use a read-only handoff file format
Label A outputs as untrusted instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, while B reads runtime files and can egress broadly. The pair only leaks if sensitive files are mounted into B's runtime or manually transferred from A to B. Because A itself has no data surface, the blast radius is limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into B's runtime volume
IF A outputs are manually copied into B and then sent over B's network egress
mitigations: Mount only non-sensitive files into B
Keep A outputs out of B's runtime volume
Restrict B network egress where possible
Rotate any API keys exposed to B
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surface, but B can write the filesystem and modify git state inside its runtime. If both are pointed at the same mounted volume or repo, B can overwrite artifacts that A conceptually owns. Uncertainty about shared storage escalates above low because B's write capabilities are explicit.
conditions: IF A and B are attached to the same mounted volume or repository
IF B is allowed to modify git state without external locking
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Mount shared paths read-only to B
Pause B before any git write
Add a lock file around shared repos
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an un-runnable curated list, so it does not generate operational facts itself; however, if its content is used as authoritative input to B, B can act on it with shell, browser, and git privileges. The interaction is indirect and not default, but B's action-taking authority makes downstream mistakes materially impactful.
conditions: IF A's text is fed into B as authoritative instructions or facts
IF B is permitted to execute shell or git actions based on that input
mitigations: Require B to verify A-derived claims before acting
Keep A as reference-only, not task input
Add a human approval step for B writes
Limit B to dry-run mode for first pass
requires-engineering: implement citation checking before actions

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source awesome list with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or retention issue. B handles files in its runtime and model-provider API keys, so compliance risk arises only if regulated data is mounted into that runtime or sent through B's configured provider. The mismatch is possible but not inherent.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into B's runtime
IF B's configured model provider stores prompts or files outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Do not mount regulated data into B
Use a provider with the required residency terms
Review retention settings before first run
Keep A free of regulated inputs
requires-engineering: add residency policy enforcement
